crossovers.thin_output_boundary: No crossover is asserted between dense metric-only output and drag/fresh factor-only output because the contracts differ.
No crossover is asserted between dense metric-only output and drag/fresh factor-only output because the contracts differ.

contract_boundary.claim_scope: Performance claims compare only dense same-output paths. Thin factor-only paths are reported separately because they return and retain a different representation.
contract_boundary.steady_state_representation_boundary: The dense metric path begins from stored (L, Aw); drag paths begin from stored (L, Vb, Vc). Initial factor solves, initial dense materialization, and conversion between these persistent representations are excluded. This is a steady-state representation comparison, not a same-input kernel dispatcher benchmark.

protocol.confirmation_outcome_blinding: Do not inspect or report partial confirmation outcomes. Inspect results only after the full grid and strict audit complete.
protocol.correctness_reference: Fresh FP64 Cholesky of G+zz^T, fresh triangular solves for B and C, and direct double-sided whitening of M=B C^T.
protocol.crossover_definition: For each rank, the crossover is the first tested factor width p for which the aggregate median metric-only-specialized time is no greater than the aggregate median alternative time. Equivalently, alternative/metric is at least one. Report both the first tested winning width and the bracketing interval from the previous tested width.

development_selection.selected_materialization: single-thread torch.mm(out=...) for every tested width

protocol.objective: Confirm the dense metric-only specialization against a fairly optimized one-sided drag-plus-materialization baseline while preserving the thin-factor output boundary.

drag_factor_only.description: Selected fair row-major/caller-workspace one-sided update without materializing Aw.

drag_materialize.description: Selected fair row-major/caller-workspace one-sided update followed by single-thread MKL materialization into caller-owned dense output.

fresh_factor_only.description: Fresh Cholesky and two thin triangular solves without materializing Aw.

fresh_materialize.description: Fresh Cholesky, two thin triangular solves, and single-thread MKL materialization into caller-owned dense output.

generic_w0_ablation.description: Same extension and ownership as the specialization, but executes the general zero-RHS solve and null dense correction.

metric_only_specialized.description: In-place L and Aw update; omits v_w, v_z, and the identically zero outer-product correction.

primary_estimands: Within-seed median drag-plus-materialization time divided by within-seed median metric-only-specialized time; a ratio greater than one favors the metric-only specialization.
Within-seed median fresh-plus-materialization time divided by within-seed median metric-only-specialized time; a ratio greater than one favors the metric-only specialization.

source_lock.mechanism: The submitted SOURCE_COMMIT must equal detached Git HEAD; tracked worktree and index must be clean before build and execution.

protocol.state_preparation: All mutable input cloning, caller-owned update workspace creation, and caller-owned dense output creation occur before each timed interval.
protocol.statistical_unit: One independently generated problem seed; repeat-level timings are summarized within seed and are not pseudoreplicated.
protocol.steady_state_representation_boundary: The dense metric path begins from stored (L, Aw); drag paths begin from stored (L, Vb, Vc). Initial factor solves, initial dense materialization, and conversion between these persistent representations are excluded. This is a steady-state representation comparison, not a same-input kernel dispatcher benchmark.
protocol.stopping_rule: Run every declared rank, width, seed, path, warmup, and timing repetition. Do not tune, filter, stop, or rerun based on confirmation outcomes.
protocol.timing_order: Every repetition contains every path once. The six-path order is cyclically rotated by (seed + width_index + repetition) modulo six, so each path occupies every timing position exactly five times.
